judge.notes: The core orchestration logic is highly faithful: validation bounds (DT-V), risk banding thresholds (DT-S, including exact inclusive boundaries), pricing formula and operation order (DT-P: surcharge before multiplier), and all four failure paths (invalid request, store failure, screening outage, notification fire-and-forget) are implemented correctly and match the worked examples. Relationships between the five backend elements are all realized in call structure. However, the code is a plain in-memory Python simulation with zero reflection of any declared technology (FastAPI, PostgreSQL, REST/HTTPS, SQL/TCP) in naming, interfaces, or comments — none of the 8 technology annotations are honored, and there is no HTTP layer or persistence layer at all. The Shipper actor/caller is not modeled explicitly, only implied via the top-level handle() function. Business-logic invention is present but narrow: a hidden default risk index of 0 when the caller supplies none, and a generic catch-all exception path that emits status strings never present in the API contract's enum, both of which deviate from or extend the specified state space. The ad hoc sentinel-based fault-injection interface is a further invented protocol, albeit primarily serving as test scaffolding rather than end-user-facing business logic. Overall a structurally and numerically faithful implementation of the decision semantics, undermined by complete absence of technology realization and a few unauthorized behavioral additions.
